quiz.q: {警察官|けいさつかん}にある＿＿{不正|ふせい}が{発覚|はっかく}した。
quiz.en: Misconduct unacceptable for a police officer came to light.

quiz.q: {子供|こども}を{見捨|みす}てるなど、{親|おや}としてある＿＿ことだ。
quiz.en: Abandoning a child is unthinkable for a parent.

meaning: will surely ~ / cannot help but cause ~
structure: Verb (ない form minus ない) + ずにはおかない  (する → せずにはおかない)
explain: Something naturally causes a feeling or reaction, or someone is determined to do something. It is often used with feelings like {感動|かんどう}させる. Compare ずにはすまない, which means "must do it because of duty."

examples.jp: この{映画|えいが}は{見|み}る{人|ひと}を{感動|かんどう}させずにはおかない。
examples.en: This movie is sure to move everyone who sees it.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{発言|はつげん}は{議論|ぎろん}を{呼|よ}ばずにはおかないだろう。
examples.en: His remark is sure to cause debate.

examples.jp: {今度|こんど}こそ{真実|しんじつ}を{話|はな}させずにはおかない。
examples.en: This time I will make him tell the truth, no matter what.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}の{歌声|うたごえ}は{聞|き}く{人|ひと}を{魅了|みりょう}せ＿＿。
quiz.en: Her singing voice is sure to charm everyone who hears it.

quiz.q: その{事件|じけん}は{社会|しゃかい}に{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}え＿＿だろう。
quiz.en: That incident will surely have a big impact on society.

quiz.q: {必|かなら}ず{犯人|はんにん}を{見|み}つけ{出|だ}さ＿＿。
quiz.en: I'll find the criminal, no matter what.

structure: Verb (ない form minus ない) + ずにはすまない / ないではすまない
explain: Because of the situation, rules, or duty, you cannot avoid doing something. Often used with {謝|あやま}る or {払|はら}う. Compare ずにはおかない, which is about strong will or a natural effect.

examples.jp: {人|ひと}のものを{壊|こわ}したのだから、{弁償|べんしょう}せずにはすまない。
examples.en: I broke someone's thing, so I have to pay for it.

examples.jp: こんなミスをしたら、{上司|じょうし}に{報告|ほうこく}しないではすまない。
examples.en: After such a mistake, I can't avoid reporting it to my boss.

examples.jp: {約束|やくそく}を{破|やぶ}ったのだから、{謝|あやま}らずにはすまないだろう。
examples.en: You broke your promise, so you will have to apologize.

quiz.q: {会社|かいしゃ}に{損害|そんがい}を{与|あた}えたのだから、{責任|せきにん}を{取|と}ら＿＿。
quiz.en: Since you caused damage to the company, you must take responsibility.

quiz.q: {部長|ぶちょう}の{車|くるま}にぶつけたのだから、{謝|あやま}ら＿＿だろう。
quiz.en: You hit the manager's car, so you'll have to apologize.

quiz.q: {法律|ほうりつ}が{変|か}わった{以上|いじょう}、{制度|せいど}を{見直|みなお}さ＿＿。
quiz.en: Now that the law has changed, the system has to be reviewed.

structure: Noun (feeling) + を{禁|きん}じ{得|え}ない
explain: A formal way to say you cannot hold back a feeling, like anger, tears, or surprise. It is used with feeling nouns such as {怒|いか}り, {涙|なみだ}, {同情|どうじょう}. It is not used for actions.

examples.jp: その{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いて、{涙|なみだ}を{禁|きん}じ{得|え}なかった。
examples.en: I could not hold back my tears when I heard that story.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{無責任|むせきにん}な{態度|たいど}に{怒|いか}りを{禁|きん}じ{得|え}ない。
examples.en: I can't help feeling angry at his irresponsible attitude.

examples.jp: {被害者|ひがいしゃ}の{家族|かぞく}には{同情|どうじょう}を{禁|きん}じ{得|え}ない。
examples.en: I can't help feeling sympathy for the victims' families.

quiz.q: {突然|とつぜん}の{知|し}らせに{驚|おどろ}き＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくされる
quiz.en: I can't help being surprised by the sudden news.

quiz.q: {政府|せいふ}の{対応|たいおう}には{疑問|ぎもん}＿＿。
quiz.en: I can't help having doubts about the government's response.

quiz.q: {子供|こども}たちの{笑顔|えがお}を{見|み}て、{喜|よろこ}び＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくさせた
を{皮切|かわき}りにした
を{禁|きん}じ{得|え}なかった
quiz.en: Seeing the children's smiles, I couldn't hold back my joy.

structure: Noun + を{余儀|よぎ}なくされる / を{余儀|よぎ}なくさせる
explain: Someone is forced to do something they did not want because of circumstances. される is the passive (be forced); させる means something forces it. Often used with nouns like {中止|ちゅうし} or {変更|へんこう}.

examples.jp: {大雨|おおあめ}で、{試合|しあい}は{中止|ちゅうし}を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた。
examples.en: Because of heavy rain, the match was forced to be canceled.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}はけがで{引退|いんたい}を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた。
examples.en: He was forced to retire due to an injury.

examples.jp: {不況|ふきょう}が{会社|かいしゃ}に{人員|じんいん}{削減|さくげん}を{余儀|よぎ}なくさせた。
examples.en: The recession forced the company to cut staff.

quiz.q: {台風|たいふう}のため、{飛行機|ひこうき}は{着陸|ちゃくりく}{地|ち}の{変更|へんこう}＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた
を{禁|きん}じ{得|え}なかった
をものともしなかった
quiz.en: Because of the typhoon, the plane was forced to change its landing site.

quiz.q: {資金|しきん}{不足|ぶそく}で、{計画|けいかく}は{延期|えんき}＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた
を{皮切|かわき}りにした
quiz.en: Due to a lack of funds, the plan was forced to be postponed.

quiz.q: {病気|びょうき}が{彼|かれ}に{長期|ちょうき}{入院|にゅういん}＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくさせた
を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた
quiz.en: His illness forced him into a long hospital stay.

structure: Verb (て form) + やまない
explain: Shows a strong feeling that continues, like hoping or loving. It is used with verbs such as {願|ねが}う, {祈|いの}る, {愛|あい}する. It is formal and often used in speeches.

examples.jp: {皆様|みなさま}のご{健康|けんこう}を{願|ねが}ってやみません。
examples.en: I sincerely wish you all good health.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{生涯|しょうがい}、{故郷|こきょう}を{愛|あい}してやまなかった。
examples.en: He loved his hometown all his life.

examples.jp: {平和|へいわ}な{世界|せかい}を{望|のぞ}んでやまない。
examples.en: I truly hope for a peaceful world.

quiz.q: お{二人|ふたり}の{幸|しあわ}せを{祈|いの}って＿＿。
quiz.en: I sincerely pray for your happiness.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{子供|こども}たちに{愛|あい}されて＿＿{先生|せんせい}だった。
quiz.en: She was a teacher whom the children loved deeply.

quiz.q: {皆|みな}さんのご{活躍|かつやく}を{期待|きたい}して＿＿。
quiz.en: I truly look forward to your success.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + までもない / までもなく
explain: Something is so obvious or simple that you don't need to do it. Often used with {言|い}う, {説明|せつめい}する. {言|い}うまでもなく means "needless to say."

examples.jp: そんな{簡単|かんたん}なことは、{説明|せつめい}するまでもない。
examples.en: Such a simple thing doesn't need explaining.

examples.jp: {言|い}うまでもなく、{健康|けんこう}は{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.en: Needless to say, health is important.

examples.jp: {近|ちか}いから、{車|くるま}で{行|い}くまでもない。
examples.en: It's close, so there's no need to go by car.

quiz.q: この{程度|ていど}のかすり{傷|きず}なら、{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}く＿＿。
quiz.en: With an injury this small, there's no need to go to the hospital.

quiz.q: {言|い}う＿＿、{試験|しけん}{中|ちゅう}の{携帯|けいたい}{使用|しよう}は{禁止|きんし}です。
quiz.en: Needless to say, phone use during the exam is prohibited.

quiz.q: {電話|でんわ}ですむことなので、わざわざ{会|あ}いに{行|い}く＿＿。
quiz.en: It can be handled by phone, so there's no need to go and meet in person.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + までだ / Verb (た form) + までのことだ
explain: With dictionary form, it means "if that fails, I'll simply do this other thing." With た form, it means "I only did this, nothing more." It shows a calm, decided feeling.

examples.jp: バスがないなら、{歩|ある}いて{帰|かえ}るまでだ。
examples.en: If there's no bus, I'll just walk home.

examples.jp: {反対|はんたい}されても、{一人|ひとり}でやるまでだ。
examples.en: Even if they oppose me, I'll just do it alone.

examples.jp: {当然|とうぜん}のことをしたまでです。
examples.en: I only did what was natural.

quiz.q: {今年|ことし}だめなら、{来年|らいねん}また{受験|じゅけん}する＿＿。
quiz.en: If I fail this year, I'll just take the exam again next year.

quiz.q: お{礼|れい}なんていりません。{仕事|しごと}をした＿＿ですから。
quiz.en: No need to thank me. I was only doing my job.

quiz.q: {誰|だれ}も{手伝|てつだ}ってくれないなら、{自分|じぶん}でやる＿＿。
quiz.en: If nobody will help me, I'll just do it myself.

structure: Verb (dictionary) / Noun / Adj + に{越|こ}したことはない
explain: Means "it's better if it is so," often used for common sense advice. It is softer than べきだ. It is often used with ほうがいい ideas like {安|やす}い, {早|はや}い, {注意|ちゅうい}する.

examples.jp: {値段|ねだん}は{安|やす}いに{越|こ}したことはない。
examples.en: Cheaper is always better.

examples.jp: {念|ねん}のため、{確認|かくにん}するに{越|こ}したことはない。
examples.en: Just in case, it's best to check.

examples.jp: {健康|けんこう}に{越|こ}したことはない。
examples.en: Nothing is better than good health.

quiz.q: {念|ねん}のため、{用心|ようじん}する＿＿。
options: に{越|こ}したことはない
quiz.en: Just to be safe, it's best to be careful.

quiz.q: {早|はや}めに{準備|じゅんび}する＿＿。
options: に{越|こ}したことはない
quiz.en: It's best to prepare early.

quiz.q: {貯金|ちょきん}は{多|おお}い＿＿が、{使|つか}うことも{大切|たいせつ}だ。
options: に{越|こ}したことはない
quiz.en: Having more savings is better, but spending is also important.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + にたえない / にたえる; Noun (feeling) + にたえない
explain: {見|み}る/{聞|き}くにたえない means "too bad to watch or listen to." Noun + にたえない (like {感謝|かんしゃ}にたえない) means "I feel deeply." にたえる means "worth (watching/reading)."

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{悪口|わるぐち}は{聞|き}くにたえない。
examples.en: His insults are unbearable to listen to.

examples.jp: {皆様|みなさま}のご{支援|しえん}に{感謝|かんしゃ}にたえません。
examples.en: I am deeply grateful for your support.

examples.jp: これは{大人|おとな}の{鑑賞|かんしょう}にたえる{作品|さくひん}だ。
examples.en: This work is worth appreciating even for adults.

quiz.q: {事故|じこ}{現場|げんば}は{見|み}る＿＿{状態|じょうたい}だった。
quiz.en: The accident scene was too terrible to look at.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}の{歌|うた}は{下手|へた}すぎて、{聞|き}く＿＿。
options: に{越|こ}したことはない
quiz.en: His singing is so bad it's unbearable to listen to.

quiz.q: {多|おお}くの{方|かた}のご{協力|きょうりょく}をいただき、{感謝|かんしゃ}＿＿。
quiz.en: I am deeply grateful for so many people's cooperation.

structure: Verb (dictionary) / Noun + に{足|た}る + Noun
explain: Means something is worth or good enough for an action, like trust or respect. に{足|た}らない means "not worth it." Compare にたえる, which is mostly about watching or reading.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{信頼|しんらい}するに{足|た}る{人物|じんぶつ}だ。
examples.en: He is a person worthy of trust.

examples.jp: それは{取|と}るに{足|た}らない{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.en: That is a trivial problem.

examples.jp: {満足|まんぞく}に{足|た}る{結果|けっか}が{出|で}た。
examples.en: We got a satisfying result.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{尊敬|そんけい}する＿＿{先輩|せんぱい}だ。
quiz.en: She is a senior worthy of respect.

quiz.q: そんな{取|と}る＿＿ことで{悩|なや}む{必要|ひつよう}はない。
quiz.en: You don't need to worry about such a trivial thing.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}には{信用|しんよう}する＿＿{証拠|しょうこ}がない。
quiz.en: There is no evidence that makes his story worth believing.

structure: Noun / Verb (dictionary) + にかたくない
explain: Means "it is not hard to imagine or understand." It is used with {想像|そうぞう}, {理解|りかい}, {察|さっ}する. It is formal and used in writing.

examples.jp: {家族|かぞく}を{失|うしな}った{彼|かれ}の{悲|かな}しみは、{想像|そうぞう}にかたくない。
examples.en: It is easy to imagine his sadness at losing his family.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}が{怒|おこ}った{理由|りゆう}は{理解|りかい}にかたくない。
examples.en: It is easy to understand why she got angry.

examples.jp: {親|おや}の{心配|しんぱい}は{察|さっ}するにかたくない。
examples.en: It is easy to guess how worried the parents are.

quiz.q: {一人|ひとり}で{子供|こども}を{育|そだ}てる{苦労|くろう}は、{想像|そうぞう}＿＿。
quiz.en: The hardship of raising a child alone is easy to imagine.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}がどれほど{努力|どりょく}したかは、{察|さっ}する＿＿。
options: に{越|こ}したことはない
quiz.en: It is easy to guess how hard he worked.

quiz.q: {優勝|ゆうしょう}した{時|とき}の{喜|よろこ}びは{想像|そうぞう}＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくされる
quiz.en: It is easy to imagine the joy of winning.

structure: Noun + の / Verb (dictionary) + かたわら
explain: Someone does a second activity besides their main job over a long time. Compare ながら, which is two actions at the same moment, and がてら, which is one trip with two purposes.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{会社|かいしゃ}で{働|はたら}くかたわら、{小説|しょうせつ}を{書|か}いている。
examples.en: While working at a company, he also writes novels.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{子育|こそだ}てのかたわら、{大学|だいがく}で{勉強|べんきょう}している。
examples.en: While raising children, she also studies at university.

examples.jp: {父|ちち}は{教師|きょうし}をするかたわら、{畑|はたけ}で{野菜|やさい}を{作|つく}っている。
examples.en: While working as a teacher, my father also grows vegetables.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{医者|いしゃ}の{仕事|しごと}の＿＿、ボランティア{活動|かつどう}もしている。
quiz.en: Besides his work as a doctor, he also does volunteer work.

quiz.q: {母|はは}は{家事|かじ}の＿＿、{翻訳|ほんやく}の{仕事|しごと}をしている。
quiz.en: Alongside the housework, my mother also does translation work.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{大学|だいがく}に{通|かよ}う＿＿、モデルとして{活躍|かつやく}している。
quiz.en: While attending university, she also works as a model.

meaning: while ~ (doing two things on one trip)
structure: Noun / Verb (ます stem) + がてら
explain: While doing A, you also do B, usually on the same trip. A is often a walk or outing, like {散歩|さんぽ}がてら. It is casual. Compare かたがた, which is formal.

examples.jp: {散歩|さんぽ}がてら、パンを{買|か}いに{行|い}った。
examples.en: I went to buy bread while taking a walk.

examples.jp: {駅|えき}まで{送|おく}りがてら、{本屋|ほんや}に{寄|よ}った。
examples.en: While seeing her off to the station, I stopped by a bookstore.

examples.jp: {買|か}い{物|もの}がてら、{友達|ともだち}の{家|いえ}に{寄|よ}った。
examples.en: I dropped by a friend's house while out shopping.

quiz.q: {天気|てんき}がいいので、{散歩|さんぽ}＿＿{郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}に{行|い}ってきます。
quiz.en: The weather's nice, so I'll go to the post office while taking a walk.

quiz.q: {花見|はなみ}＿＿、{公園|こうえん}でお{弁当|べんとう}を{食|た}べた。
quiz.en: While enjoying the cherry blossoms, we ate lunch in the park.

quiz.q: {運動|うんどう}＿＿、{歩|ある}いて{会社|かいしゃ}に{通|かよ}っている。
quiz.en: I walk to work, which also gives me exercise.

structure: Noun + かたがた
explain: A formal way to say you do one action with two purposes, like visiting to greet and also to thank. Used with nouns like お{礼|れい}, ご{挨拶|あいさつ}, お{見舞|みま}い. Often in letters and business.

examples.jp: お{礼|れい}かたがた、ご{挨拶|あいさつ}に{伺|うかが}いました。
examples.en: I came to greet you and also to thank you.

examples.jp: ご{報告|ほうこく}かたがた、お{礼|れい}を{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.en: I'd like to report to you and also thank you.

examples.jp: お{見舞|みま}いかたがた、{先生|せんせい}のお{宅|たく}を{訪|たず}ねた。
examples.en: I visited my teacher's home to see how he was and also to say hello.

quiz.q: {近況|きんきょう}{報告|ほうこく}＿＿、お{手紙|てがみ}を{差|さ}し{上|あ}げます。
quiz.en: I'm writing to you to let you know how I'm doing as well.

quiz.q: {就職|しゅうしょく}のご{報告|ほうこく}＿＿、{恩師|おんし}を{訪|たず}ねた。
quiz.en: I visited my former teacher to report my new job and to say hello.

quiz.q: お{詫|わ}び＿＿、ご{説明|せつめい}に{参|まい}りました。
quiz.en: I have come to apologize and also to explain.

structure: Verb (dictionary) / この / あの + {始末|しまつ}だ
explain: After a series of bad things, it finally ended in an even worse result. It shows the speaker's criticism or disappointment. Compare あげく, which is similar but less emotional.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{遅刻|ちこく}ばかりして、ついには{無断|むだん}で{休|やす}む{始末|しまつ}だ。
examples.en: He was always late, and in the end he even skipped work without telling anyone.

examples.jp: {弟|おとうと}はお{金|かね}を{使|つか}い{果|は}たし、{私|わたし}に{借|か}りに{来|く}る{始末|しまつ}だ。
examples.en: My brother spent all his money and even came to borrow from me.

examples.jp: {何度|なんど}{注意|ちゅうい}しても{直|なお}らず、この{始末|しまつ}だ。
examples.en: I warned him many times, but nothing changed, and now look at this.

quiz.q: {息子|むすこ}は{勉強|べんきょう}しないで、{最後|さいご}には{学校|がっこう}を{辞|や}める＿＿。
quiz.en: My son didn't study, and in the end he even quit school.

quiz.q: {飲|の}みすぎて、{駅|えき}で{寝|ね}てしまう＿＿だった。
quiz.en: I drank too much and ended up falling asleep at the station.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}はうそを{重|かさ}ね、とうとう{友達|ともだち}を{全員|ぜんいん}{失|うしな}う＿＿。
quiz.en: He kept lying and finally lost all his friends.

structure: Noun + ずくめ
explain: Means something is filled with only one kind of thing. It is often used with good things like いいこと or ごちそう, and with {黒|くろ} for color. Compare まみれ, which is for dirty things on a surface.

examples.jp: {今年|ことし}はいいことずくめの{一年|いちねん}だった。
examples.en: This year was full of good things.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}はいつも{黒|くろ}ずくめの{服|ふく}を{着|き}ている。
examples.en: He always wears all black.

examples.jp: {結婚式|けっこんしき}はごちそうずくめだった。
examples.en: The wedding was full of great food.

quiz.q: {昇進|しょうしん}に{結婚|けっこん}と、{最近|さいきん}はいいこと＿＿だ。
quiz.en: With a promotion and a wedding, lately everything has been good.

quiz.q: {黒|くろ}＿＿の{男|おとこ}が{立|た}っていた。
quiz.en: A man dressed all in black was standing there.

quiz.q: この{会社|かいしゃ}は{規則|きそく}＿＿で{窮屈|きゅうくつ}だ。
quiz.en: This company is full of rules and feels stifling.

structure: Noun + まみれ
explain: Means something is covered all over with a dirty or unpleasant thing, like mud, sweat, or blood. Compare だらけ, which can also mean "full of" mistakes or problems.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}たちは{泥|どろ}まみれになって{遊|あそ}んだ。
examples.en: The kids played and got covered in mud.

examples.jp: {夏|なつ}の{工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}で、{汗|あせ}まみれになって{働|はたら}いた。
examples.en: I worked at the construction site in summer, drenched in sweat.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{血|ち}まみれで{倒|たお}れていた。
examples.en: He was lying there covered in blood.

quiz.q: {大掃除|おおそうじ}をしたら、{手|て}がほこり＿＿になった。
quiz.en: After the big cleaning, my hands were covered in dust.

quiz.q: {雨|あめ}の{中|なか}で{試合|しあい}をして、{選手|せんしゅ}たちは{泥|どろ}＿＿だった。
quiz.en: After playing in the rain, the players were covered in mud.

quiz.q: {借金|しゃっきん}＿＿の{生活|せいかつ}から{抜|ぬ}け{出|だ}したい。
quiz.en: I want to escape a life buried in debt.

structure: Noun + めく / めいた + Noun
explain: Means something starts to have the feeling of a noun, like {春|はる}めく (feel like spring). めいた + noun means "sounding like," as in {皮肉|ひにく}めいた{言葉|ことば}.

examples.jp: {日差|ひざ}しが{暖|あたた}かくなって、{春|はる}めいてきた。
examples.en: The sunshine has gotten warm, and it's starting to feel like spring.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{冗談|じょうだん}めいた{口調|くちょう}で{話|はな}した。
examples.en: He spoke in a joking tone.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}の{言葉|ことば}には{皮肉|ひにく}めいたところがある。
examples.en: There is something sarcastic about her words.

quiz.q: {木々|きぎ}の{葉|は}が{色|いろ}づき、すっかり{秋|あき}＿＿きた。
quiz.en: The leaves have changed color, and it really feels like autumn now.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{言|い}い{訳|わけ}＿＿ことは{一言|ひとこと}も{言|い}わなかった。
quiz.en: He didn't say a single word that sounded like an excuse.

quiz.q: {謎|なぞ}＿＿{手紙|てがみ}が{届|とど}いた。
quiz.en: A mysterious-sounding letter arrived.

structure: Noun / な-Adj stem / い-Adj stem + ぶる
explain: Someone acts as if they are something they are not, usually in an annoying way. Common words are {偉|えら}ぶる, {上品|じょうひん}ぶる, いい{子|こ}ぶる. It has a negative feeling. Compare めく, which is about natural signs.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{新人|しんじん}なのに{先輩|せんぱい}ぶっている。
examples.en: He's a newcomer but acts like a senior.

examples.jp: {先生|せんせい}の{前|まえ}だけいい{子|こ}ぶるのはやめなさい。
examples.en: Stop acting like a good kid only in front of the teacher.

examples.jp: {偉|えら}ぶった{態度|たいど}は{嫌|きら}われる。
examples.en: People dislike a self-important attitude.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{何|なん}でも{知|し}っているかのように{学者|がくしゃ}＿＿いる。
quiz.en: She acts like a scholar, as if she knows everything.

quiz.q: {上品|じょうひん}＿＿{話|はな}し{方|かた}が{鼻|はな}につく。
quiz.en: Her affected, upper-class way of speaking is irritating.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{部長|ぶちょう}になってから{偉|えら}＿＿ようになった。
quiz.en: He started acting important after becoming manager.

structure: Verb (dictionary) / Noun + の + きらいがある
explain: Someone has a tendency to do something bad or undesirable. It is used for criticism. Compare がちだ, which is softer and more common in daily speech.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{物事|ものごと}を{大|おお}げさに{言|い}うきらいがある。
examples.en: He tends to exaggerate things.

examples.jp: {最近|さいきん}の{若者|わかもの}は{失敗|しっぱい}を{恐|おそ}れるきらいがある。
examples.en: Young people today tend to be afraid of failure.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{何|なん}でも{一人|ひとり}で{決|き}めてしまうきらいがある。
examples.en: She tends to decide everything on her own.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{人|ひと}の{意見|いけん}を{聞|き}かない＿＿。
quiz.en: He tends not to listen to others' opinions.

quiz.q: {政府|せいふ}は{問題|もんだい}を{先送|さきおく}りにする＿＿。
quiz.en: The government tends to postpone problems.

quiz.q: {父|ちち}は{少|すこ}し{頑固|がんこ}な＿＿。
quiz.en: My father tends to be a bit stubborn.

structure: Noun + の + ごとき + Noun / ごとく + Verb; Noun + ごとき (humble or scornful)
explain: A formal way to say ような or ように. ごとく is used before a verb and ごとき before a noun. Noun + ごとき (without の) can also look down on someone, like {私|わたし}ごとき "someone like me."

examples.jp: {時間|じかん}は{矢|や}のごとく{過|す}ぎていく。
examples.en: Time flies like an arrow.

examples.jp: {前述|ぜんじゅつ}のごとく、{計画|けいかく}は{変更|へんこう}された。
examples.en: As stated above, the plan was changed.

examples.jp: {私|わたし}ごときに、そんな{大役|たいやく}は{務|つと}まりません。
examples.en: Someone like me can't handle such an important role.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{何事|なにごと}もなかったかの＿＿{笑|わら}っていた。
quiz.en: He was smiling as if nothing had happened.

quiz.q: {夢|ゆめ}の＿＿{日々|ひび}が{終|お}わった。
quiz.en: The dreamlike days came to an end.

quiz.q: お{前|まえ}＿＿に{負|ま}けるわけがない。
quiz.en: There's no way I'd lose to the likes of you.

structure: Verb (ない form) + までも
explain: Means "even if you can't do the full thing, at least do a smaller thing." The second part is often a lower goal with べきだ or ほしい. Compare までもない, which means "no need to."

examples.jp: {毎日|まいにち}とは{言|い}わないまでも、{週|しゅう}に{一度|いちど}は{電話|でんわ}してほしい。
examples.en: Not every day, but I want you to call at least once a week.

examples.jp: {優勝|ゆうしょう}できないまでも、{決勝|けっしょう}には{進|すす}みたい。
examples.en: Even if we can't win, I want to reach the final.

examples.jp: {謝|あやま}らないまでも、{説明|せつめい}ぐらいはするべきだ。
examples.en: Even if you don't apologize, you should at least explain.

quiz.q: {完璧|かんぺき}とは{言|い}わ＿＿、もう{少|すこ}し{丁寧|ていねい}に{書|か}いてほしい。
quiz.en: I don't ask for perfect, but I want you to write a bit more carefully.

quiz.q: {手伝|てつだ}わ＿＿、{邪魔|じゃま}はしないでほしい。
quiz.en: Even if you don't help, at least don't get in the way.

quiz.q: {満点|まんてん}は{取|と}れ＿＿、{合格|ごうかく}{点|てん}は{取|と}りたい。
quiz.en: Even if I can't get full marks, I want a passing score.

structure: Verb (ない form) + ものでもない
explain: Means "I might do it, depending on the situation." It is an indirect, slightly reluctant yes. ないでもない is a similar, softer form.

examples.jp: {条件|じょうけん}によっては、{引|ひ}き{受|う}けないものでもない。
examples.en: Depending on the conditions, I might take it on.

examples.jp: {急|いそ}げば、{間|ま}に{合|あ}わないものでもない。
examples.en: If we hurry, we might make it.

examples.jp: {頼|たの}まれれば、{手伝|てつだ}わないものでもない。
examples.en: If asked, I might help.

quiz.q: {給料|きゅうりょう}が{上|あ}がるなら、{転勤|てんきん}し＿＿。
quiz.en: If my salary goes up, I might accept the transfer.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}が{謝|あやま}るなら、{許|ゆる}さ＿＿。
quiz.en: If he apologizes, I might forgive him.

quiz.q: {今|いま}から{始|はじ}めれば、{完成|かんせい}し＿＿が、{厳|きび}しいだろう。
quiz.en: If we start now, we might finish it, but it'll be tough.

structure: Verb (ない form minus ない) + ずじまい  (する → せずじまい)
explain: You wanted to do something, but in the end you never did it and now it's too late. It shows regret. Compare ないで{終|お}わる, which is plainer.

examples.jp: {忙|いそが}しくて、{旅行|りょこう}には{行|い}かずじまいだった。
examples.en: I was busy, so I never ended up going on the trip.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}の{名前|なまえ}は{聞|き}かずじまいだった。
examples.en: I never got to ask her name.

examples.jp: {買|か}った{本|ほん}を{読|よ}まずじまいで{捨|す}ててしまった。
examples.en: I threw away the book I bought without ever reading it.

quiz.q: {日本|にほん}にいる{間|あいだ}に{富士山|ふじさん}に{登|のぼ}りたかったが、{登|のぼ}ら＿＿だった。
quiz.en: I wanted to climb Mt. Fuji while in Japan, but I never did.

quiz.q: {結局|けっきょく}、{本当|ほんとう}の{理由|りゆう}は{分|わ}から＿＿だった。
quiz.en: In the end, I never found out the real reason.

quiz.q: お{礼|れい}を{言|い}おうと{思|おも}っていたのに、{言|い}わ＿＿になってしまった。
quiz.en: I meant to thank her, but I never did.

structure: Verb (ない form minus ない) + んばかりに / んばかりの + Noun  (する → せんばかり)
explain: Means something looks so strong that it seems about to happen, though it doesn't really. Used for strong feelings or states, like {泣|な}かんばかり. Compare とばかりに, which is about attitude, as if saying something.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{泣|な}き{出|だ}さんばかりの{顔|かお}をしていた。
examples.en: She looked as if she was about to cry.

examples.jp: {会場|かいじょう}は{割|わ}れんばかりの{拍手|はくしゅ}に{包|つつ}まれた。
examples.en: The hall was filled with thunderous applause.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{飛|と}び{上|あ}がらんばかりに{喜|よろこ}んだ。
examples.en: He was so happy he almost jumped.

quiz.q: {犬|いぬ}はしっぽがちぎれ＿＿に{振|ふ}っていた。
quiz.en: The dog was wagging its tail so hard it looked like it would fall off.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{今|いま}にも{殴|なぐ}りかから＿＿{勢|いきお}いで{怒|おこ}った。
quiz.en: He got angry as if he was about to hit someone.

quiz.q: {母|はは}は{私|わたし}の{合格|ごうかく}を{聞|き}いて、{踊|おど}り{出|だ}さ＿＿に{喜|よろこ}んだ。
quiz.en: My mother was so happy at my passing that she nearly started dancing.

structure: plain form / phrase + とばかりに
explain: Someone doesn't say it out loud, but their action clearly shows they mean it. Compare んばかり, which describes a state that seems about to happen.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は「{出|で}ていけ」とばかりにドアを{開|あ}けた。
examples.en: He opened the door as if to say "Get out."

examples.jp: {子供|こども}は「{待|ま}ってました」とばかりにケーキに{手|て}を{伸|の}ばした。
examples.en: The child reached for the cake as if to say "Finally!"

examples.jp: {店員|てんいん}は{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}れとばかりに{片付|かたづ}けを{始|はじ}めた。
examples.en: The staff started cleaning up as if telling us to leave.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は「もう{知|し}らない」＿＿{横|よこ}を{向|む}いた。
quiz.en: She turned away as if to say "I don't care anymore."

quiz.q: チャンス＿＿、{彼|かれ}は{一気|いっき}に{攻|せ}めた。
quiz.en: As if it were his chance, he attacked all at once.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は「{当然|とうぜん}だ」＿＿{胸|むね}を{張|は}った。
quiz.en: He puffed out his chest as if to say "Of course."

meaning: extremely ~ / so ~ you can't describe it
structure: Noun / い-Adj (dictionary) + といったらない / ったらない
explain: Means a feeling or state is so strong it can't be put into words. It can be positive or negative. ったらない is the casual form.

examples.jp: {試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}した{時|とき}のうれしさといったらなかった。
examples.en: I can't describe how happy I was when I passed the exam.

examples.jp: {満員|まんいん}{電車|でんしゃ}の{苦|くる}しさといったらない。
examples.en: Packed trains are unbearably uncomfortable.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{部屋|へや}の{汚|きたな}さったらない。
examples.en: His room is incredibly dirty.

quiz.q: {初|はじ}めて{見|み}た{富士山|ふじさん}の{美|うつく}しさ＿＿。
quiz.en: Words can't describe the beauty of Mt. Fuji when I first saw it.

quiz.q: {一人|ひとり}で{過|す}ごす{夜|よる}の{寂|さび}しさ＿＿。
quiz.en: Nights spent alone are unbearably lonely.

quiz.q: スピーチで{名前|なまえ}を{間違|まちが}えた{時|とき}の{恥|は}ずかしさ＿＿。
quiz.en: I can't describe how embarrassed I was when I got the name wrong in my speech.

structure: な-Adj stem + {極|きわ}まりない / {極|きわ}まる
explain: Means "extremely," usually for negative states like {失礼|しつれい} or {危険|きけん}. It is formal and strong. Both forms have the same meaning.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{態度|たいど}は{失礼|しつれい}{極|きわ}まりない。
examples.en: His attitude is extremely rude.

examples.jp: {夜道|よみち}を{一人|ひとり}で{歩|ある}くのは{危険|きけん}{極|きわ}まりない。
examples.en: Walking alone at night is extremely dangerous.

examples.jp: {退屈|たいくつ}{極|きわ}まる{会議|かいぎ}だった。
examples.en: It was an extremely boring meeting.

quiz.q: {運転中|うんてんちゅう}にスマホを{見|み}るなんて、{危険|きけん}＿＿。
quiz.en: Looking at your phone while driving is extremely dangerous.

quiz.q: {約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}に{連絡|れんらく}もなく{来|こ}ないとは、{非常識|ひじょうしき}＿＿。
quiz.en: Not showing up or calling at the promised time is extremely thoughtless.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}の{説明|せつめい}は{不親切|ふしんせつ}＿＿ものだった。
quiz.en: His explanation was extremely unhelpful.

structure: Noun + の{至|いた}り
explain: Means the highest degree of a feeling. It is very formal and often used in speeches, like {光栄|こうえい}の{至|いた}り. {若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}り means "a mistake of youth."

examples.jp: このような{賞|しょう}をいただき、{光栄|こうえい}の{至|いた}りです。
examples.en: It is a great honor to receive such an award.

examples.jp: {皆様|みなさま}にお{会|あ}いでき、{感激|かんげき}の{至|いた}りです。
examples.en: I am deeply moved to meet you all.

examples.jp: あれは{若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}りだった。
examples.en: That was a youthful mistake.

quiz.q: {先生|せんせい}にお{褒|ほ}めいただき、{恐縮|きょうしゅく}＿＿です。
quiz.en: I am truly humbled by your praise.

quiz.q: {大切|たいせつ}な{会議|かいぎ}に{遅|おく}れるとは、{不徳|ふとく}＿＿です。
quiz.en: Being late for an important meeting is entirely my fault.

quiz.q: {世界的|せかいてき}な{方|かた}とご{一緒|いっしょ}でき、{光栄|こうえい}＿＿です。
quiz.en: It is a great honor to be with someone so world-famous.

structure: Noun + の{極|きわ}み
explain: Means the highest point of something, often a feeling or a state. It is formal. Common phrases are {贅沢|ぜいたく}の{極|きわ}み, {疲労|ひろう}の{極|きわ}み, and {痛恨|つうこん}の{極|きわ}み.

examples.jp: {海|うみ}を{見|み}ながら{温泉|おんせん}に{入|はい}るのは{贅沢|ぜいたく}の{極|きわ}みだ。
examples.en: Soaking in a hot spring while looking at the sea is the height of luxury.

examples.jp: {徹夜|てつや}が{続|つづ}いて{疲労|ひろう}の{極|きわ}みに{達|たっ}した。
examples.en: After many all-nighters, I reached total exhaustion.

examples.jp: {決勝|けっしょう}で{負|ま}けたのは{痛恨|つうこん}の{極|きわ}みだ。
examples.en: Losing in the final is deeply painful.

quiz.q: このような{事態|じたい}を{招|まね}き、{遺憾|いかん}＿＿です。
quiz.en: We deeply regret causing this situation.

quiz.q: {高級|こうきゅう}ホテルのスイートに{泊|と}まるなんて、{贅沢|ぜいたく}＿＿だ。
quiz.en: Staying in a suite at a luxury hotel is the height of luxury.

quiz.q: {三日|みっか}{寝|ね}ずに{働|はたら}いて、{疲労|ひろう}＿＿に{達|たっ}した。
quiz.en: After working three days without sleep, I reached total exhaustion.

meaning: if ~, that's the end of it
structure: Verb (ば form) + それまでだ
explain: Means "if this happens, everything is over and it was all for nothing." It is often used for warnings. Compare までだ, which shows a calm decision.

examples.jp: どんなに{頑張|がんば}っても、{試験|しけん}に{落|お}ちればそれまでだ。
examples.en: No matter how hard you try, if you fail the exam, that's it.

examples.jp: {高|たか}いカメラも、{落|お}として{壊|こわ}せばそれまでだ。
examples.en: Even an expensive camera is useless if you drop and break it.

examples.jp: {才能|さいのう}があっても、{努力|どりょく}しなければそれまでだ。
examples.en: Even with talent, if you don't make an effort, that's the end of it.

quiz.q: {貯金|ちょきん}しても、{病気|びょうき}になれ＿＿。
quiz.en: Even with savings, if you get sick, it's all over.

quiz.q: {計画|けいかく}がよくても、{実行|じっこう}しなけれ＿＿。
quiz.en: Even a good plan is worthless if you don't carry it out.

quiz.q: データも、バックアップがなく{消|き}えてしまえ＿＿。
quiz.en: If data vanishes with no backup, that's the end of it.

meaning: it's not like ~ / since it isn't ~
structure: Noun + ではあるまいし / じゃあるまいし
explain: Means "it's not as if (something obvious), so (criticism or advice)." It is used to scold or point out that someone is acting silly. じゃあるまいし is casual.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}ではあるまいし、{自分|じぶん}でやりなさい。
examples.en: You're not a child, so do it yourself.

examples.jp: {一生|いっしょう}の{別|わか}れじゃあるまいし、そんなに{泣|な}かないで。
examples.en: It's not like we'll never meet again, so don't cry so much.

examples.jp: {神様|かみさま}ではあるまいし、{未来|みらい}のことは{分|わ}からない。
examples.en: I'm not a god, so I can't know the future.

quiz.q: {初心者|しょしんしゃ}＿＿、そんなミスをしてはだめだ。
quiz.en: You're not a beginner, so you shouldn't make such a mistake.

quiz.q: {外国|がいこく}に{行|い}くわけ＿＿、そんなに{荷物|にもつ}はいらないよ。
quiz.en: It's not like you're going abroad, so you don't need so much luggage.

quiz.q: {泥棒|どろぼう}＿＿、こそこそしないで{入|はい}ってきなさい。
quiz.en: You're not a thief, so come in without sneaking around.

structure: Noun + なくして（は）～ない
explain: Means "without A, B cannot happen." A is something very important, like {努力|どりょく} or {協力|きょうりょく}. It is formal. Compare なしに, which can simply mean "without doing."

examples.jp: {努力|どりょく}なくして{成功|せいこう}はない。
examples.en: There is no success without effort.

examples.jp: {皆様|みなさま}のご{協力|きょうりょく}なくしては、この{計画|けいかく}は{実現|じつげん}できませんでした。
examples.en: Without your cooperation, this plan could not have been realized.

examples.jp: {愛|あい}なくして{人|ひと}は{生|い}きられない。
examples.en: People cannot live without love.

quiz.q: {両親|りょうしん}の{支|ささ}え＿＿、{今|いま}の{私|わたし}はなかった。
quiz.en: Without my parents' support, I would not be who I am today.

quiz.q: {信頼|しんらい}{関係|かんけい}＿＿、いい{仕事|しごと}はできない。
quiz.en: Without trust, you can't do good work.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}の{活躍|かつやく}＿＿、チームの{優勝|ゆうしょう}はありえなかった。
quiz.en: Without his performance, the team's win would not have been possible.

title_raw: ～いかんで / いかんによっては
structure: Noun + （の）いかんで / いかんによっては
explain: A formal way to say "depending on." The result changes based on A. いかんによっては means "depending on it, possibly (a special result)." Compare しだいで, which is less formal.

examples.jp: {結果|けっか}いかんで、{次|つぎ}の{計画|けいかく}が{決|き}まる。
examples.en: The next plan will be decided depending on the results.

examples.jp: {成績|せいせき}のいかんによっては、{進級|しんきゅう}できないこともある。
examples.en: Depending on your grades, you may not be able to move up a year.

examples.jp: {天候|てんこう}いかんでは、{出発|しゅっぱつ}が{遅|おく}れる。
examples.en: Depending on the weather, departure may be delayed.

quiz.q: {本人|ほんにん}の{努力|どりょく}＿＿、{合格|ごうかく}の{可能性|かのうせい}は{十分|じゅうぶん}ある。
quiz.en: Depending on his own effort, he has a good chance of passing.

quiz.q: {交渉|こうしょう}の{結果|けっか}＿＿、{契約|けいやく}を{打|う}ち{切|き}ることもある。
quiz.en: Depending on the negotiation results, we may end the contract.

quiz.q: {説明|せつめい}の{仕方|しかた}＿＿、{相手|あいて}の{受|う}け{取|と}り{方|かた}は{変|か}わる。
quiz.en: How the other person takes it changes depending on how you explain.

structure: Noun + の + いかんにかかわらず / いかんによらず / いかんを{問|と}わず
explain: A formal way to say "no matter what A is, the result is the same." It is the opposite of いかんで. Often used in notices and rules.

examples.jp: {理由|りゆう}のいかんにかかわらず、{遅刻|ちこく}は{認|みと}めません。
examples.en: Regardless of the reason, lateness is not accepted.

examples.jp: {結果|けっか}のいかんによらず、{連絡|れんらく}します。
examples.en: We will contact you regardless of the result.

examples.jp: {国籍|こくせき}のいかんを{問|と}わず、{誰|だれ}でも{応募|おうぼ}できる。
examples.en: Anyone can apply, regardless of nationality.

quiz.q: {天候|てんこう}の＿＿、{大会|たいかい}は{予定|よてい}{通|どお}り{行|おこな}う。
quiz.en: Regardless of the weather, the tournament will be held as planned.

quiz.q: {購入|こうにゅう}{後|ご}は、{理由|りゆう}の＿＿、どんな{場合|ばあい}も{返品|へんぴん}できません。
quiz.en: After purchase, returns are not accepted for any reason.

quiz.q: {年齢|ねんれい}の＿＿、{参加|さんか}{費|ひ}は{同|おな}じです。
quiz.en: The participation fee is the same regardless of age.

structure: Noun + にかこつけて
explain: Someone uses a reason as an excuse to do what they really want. It has a slightly critical feeling. Compare をいいことに, which is about taking advantage of a situation.

examples.jp: {出張|しゅっちょう}にかこつけて、{観光|かんこう}を{楽|たの}しんだ。
examples.en: Using the business trip as an excuse, I enjoyed sightseeing.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{体調|たいちょう}{不良|ふりょう}にかこつけて、{会議|かいぎ}を{休|やす}んだ。
examples.en: He used feeling unwell as an excuse to skip the meeting.

examples.jp: {仕事|しごと}にかこつけて、{家事|かじ}を{手伝|てつだ}わない。
examples.en: He uses work as an excuse not to help with the housework.

quiz.q: {友達|ともだち}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}＿＿、{自分|じぶん}も{高|たか}いケーキを{食|た}べた。
quiz.en: Using a friend's birthday as an excuse, I also ate expensive cake.

quiz.q: {雨|あめ}＿＿、{彼|かれ}はジョギングをさぼった。
quiz.en: He used the rain as an excuse to skip jogging.

quiz.q: {父|ちち}は{接待|せったい}＿＿、{毎晩|まいばん}お{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}んでいる。
quiz.en: Using business entertaining as an excuse, my father drinks every night.

meaning: being too busy with ~ (to do other things)
structure: Noun + にかまけて
explain: Because someone is too focused on one thing, they neglect other important things. It shows regret or criticism. Compare にかこつけて, which is about using an excuse.

examples.jp: {仕事|しごと}にかまけて、{家族|かぞく}との{時間|じかん}を{大切|たいせつ}にしなかった。
examples.en: Too busy with work, I didn't value time with my family.

examples.jp: ゲームにかまけて、{宿題|しゅくだい}を{忘|わす}れた。
examples.en: I was so into games that I forgot my homework.

examples.jp: {子育|こそだ}てにかまけて、{自分|じぶん}のことは{後回|あとまわ}しだ。
examples.en: Busy raising children, I put myself last.

quiz.q: {部活|ぶかつ}＿＿、{勉強|べんきょう}がおろそかになった。
quiz.en: Too focused on club activities, I neglected my studies.

quiz.q: {忙|いそが}しさ＿＿、{友人|ゆうじん}に{連絡|れんらく}していない。
quiz.en: Caught up in being busy, I haven't contacted my friends.

quiz.q: {趣味|しゅみ}＿＿、{部屋|へや}の{掃除|そうじ}をしていない。
quiz.en: I'm so wrapped up in my hobby that I haven't cleaned my room.

structure: Noun + を{踏|ふ}まえて
explain: Means you use facts or past results as a base for the next step. It is formal and common at work. Compare をもとに, which is more general.

examples.jp: {前回|ぜんかい}の{反省|はんせい}を{踏|ふ}まえて、{計画|けいかく}を{見直|みなお}した。
examples.en: We reviewed the plan, taking last time's lessons into account.

examples.jp: {調査|ちょうさ}{結果|けっか}を{踏|ふ}まえて、{新|あたら}しい{商品|しょうひん}を{開発|かいはつ}する。
examples.en: We will develop new products based on the survey results.

examples.jp: {皆|みな}さんの{意見|いけん}を{踏|ふ}まえて{決|き}めます。
examples.en: We will decide taking everyone's opinions into account.

quiz.q: {過去|かこ}のデータ＿＿、{今年|ことし}の{目標|もくひょう}を{立|た}てた。
quiz.en: We set this year's goals based on past data.

quiz.q: {現状|げんじょう}＿＿、{対策|たいさく}を{考|かんが}える{必要|ひつよう}がある。
quiz.en: We need to consider measures that take the current situation into account.

quiz.q: お{客様|きゃくさま}の{声|こえ}＿＿、サービスを{改善|かいぜん}しました。
quiz.en: We improved our service based on customer feedback.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + ともなく / ともなしに
explain: Someone does something without any clear intention. It is used with verbs like {見|み}る, {聞|き}く, {考|かんが}える. With question words, like どこからともなく, it means "from somewhere unknown."

examples.jp: テレビを{見|み}るともなく{見|み}ていた。
examples.en: I was watching TV without really watching it.

examples.jp: {聞|き}くともなしに、{隣|となり}の{話|はなし}が{聞|き}こえてきた。
examples.en: Without meaning to listen, I overheard the conversation next to me.

examples.jp: どこからともなく、いい{匂|にお}いがしてきた。
examples.en: A nice smell came from somewhere.

quiz.q: {窓|まど}の{外|そと}を{眺|なが}める＿＿{眺|なが}めていた。
quiz.en: I was gazing out the window without really looking.

quiz.q: {誰|だれ}から＿＿、{拍手|はくしゅ}が{起|お}こった。
quiz.en: Applause broke out, started by no one in particular.

quiz.q: {考|かんが}える＿＿{考|かんが}えていたら、いいアイデアが{浮|う}かんだ。
quiz.en: While idly thinking, a good idea came to me.

structure: Noun / plain form + なりに / なりの + Noun
explain: Means "within one's own limits or level, doing one's best." It is often used as {私|わたし}なりに or {子供|こども}なりに. Compare ならでは, which shows something unique and special.

examples.jp: {私|わたし}なりに{頑張|がんば}ったつもりです。
examples.en: I think I did my best in my own way.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}は{子供|こども}なりに{悩|なや}みがある。
examples.en: Children have their own worries.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}には{彼|かれ}なりの{考|かんが}えがあるのだろう。
examples.en: He probably has his own way of thinking.

quiz.q: {初心者|しょしんしゃ}は{初心者|しょしんしゃ}＿＿、できることがある。
quiz.en: Even beginners have things they can do in their own way.

quiz.q: {狭|せま}いなら{狭|せま}い＿＿{工夫|くふう}がある。
quiz.en: If it's small, there are ways to make it work in its own way.

quiz.q: {自分|じぶん}＿＿の{答|こた}えを{見|み}つけたい。
quiz.en: I want to find my own answer.

meaning: because (of how it looks to others) ~
structure: Noun + の / plain form + {手前|てまえ}
explain: Means "because of my position or what I said, I have to act a certain way." It is about saving face in front of others. Compare から, which is a simple reason.

examples.jp: {行|い}くと{言|い}った{手前|てまえ}、{今更|いまさら}{断|ことわ}れない。
examples.en: Since I said I'd go, I can't back out now.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}の{手前|てまえ}、{親|おや}が{喧嘩|けんか}するわけにはいかない。
examples.en: In front of the kids, parents can't fight.

examples.jp: {先生|せんせい}の{手前|てまえ}、{知|し}らないとは{言|い}えなかった。
examples.en: In front of the teacher, I couldn't say I didn't know.

quiz.q: {自分|じぶん}から{言|い}い{出|だ}した＿＿、{途中|とちゅう}でやめるわけにはいかない。
quiz.en: Since it was my idea, I can't quit halfway.

quiz.q: {部下|ぶか}の＿＿、{上司|じょうし}として{弱音|よわね}は{吐|は}けない。
quiz.en: In front of my staff, I can't complain as their boss.

quiz.q: {必|かなら}ず{勝|か}つと{宣言|せんげん}した＿＿、{負|ま}けられない。
quiz.en: Since I declared I'd win, I can't lose.

structure: Verb (た form) + ところで
explain: Means "even if you do this, it won't help or the result will be small." The second part is negative or shows little effect. Compare ても, which is neutral.

examples.jp: {今|いま}から{急|いそ}いだところで、{間|ま}に{合|あ}わないだろう。
examples.en: Even if we hurry now, we probably won't make it.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}に{相談|そうだん}したところで、{解決|かいけつ}しない。
examples.en: Even if I ask him, it won't be solved.

examples.jp: {謝|あやま}ったところで、{許|ゆる}してもらえないだろう。
examples.en: Even if I apologize, I probably won't be forgiven.

quiz.q: {後悔|こうかい}した＿＿、{過去|かこ}は{変|か}えられない。
quiz.en: Even if you regret it, you can't change the past.

quiz.q: {高|たか}い{薬|くすり}を{買|か}った＿＿、すぐには{治|なお}らない。
quiz.en: Even if you buy expensive medicine, you won't get better right away.

quiz.q: どんなに{説明|せつめい}した＿＿、{彼|かれ}は{分|わ}かってくれないだろう。
quiz.en: No matter how much I explain, he probably won't understand.

structure: Noun + ならいざしらず
explain: Means "A might be an exception, but B is different and should be okay or should do better." It is used to compare a special case with the current case, often with criticism.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}ならいざしらず、{大人|おとな}がそんなことで{泣|な}くなんて。
examples.en: A child maybe, but an adult crying over that?

examples.jp: {昔|むかし}ならいざしらず、{今|いま}はスマホで{何|なん}でも{調|しら}べられる。
examples.en: Maybe not in the old days, but now you can look up anything on a phone.

examples.jp: {素人|しろうと}ならいざしらず、プロがこんなミスをするとは。
examples.en: An amateur maybe, but I can't believe a pro made this mistake.

quiz.q: {新人|しんじん}＿＿、{十年|じゅうねん}も{働|はたら}いていて{知|し}らないのはおかしい。
quiz.en: A newcomer maybe, but it's strange not to know after working ten years.

quiz.q: {平日|へいじつ}＿＿、{日曜日|にちようび}まで{仕事|しごと}とは{大変|たいへん}だ。
quiz.en: Weekdays are one thing, but working even on Sundays is tough.

quiz.q: {一度|いちど}＿＿、{何度|なんど}も{同|おな}じミスをするのは{困|こま}る。
quiz.en: Once would be one thing, but making the same mistake many times is a problem.
